instruction:
Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric structural model of a thick-walled cylinder under internal pressure.

Physical problem:
Axisymmetric thick-walled cylinder under internal pressure.

Coordinate system and geometry:
- Use the global Cartesian coordinate system for the axisymmetric cross-section.
- X is the radial direction.
- Y is the axial direction.
- The cylinder has an inner diameter of 50 mm and an outer diameter of 100 mm.
- Therefore, model the radial domain from X = 25 mm to X = 50 mm.
- The axial thickness is 10 mm.
- Model the rectangular axisymmetric cross-section:
  - 25 ≤ X ≤ 50 mm
  - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 mm
- Do not model or constrain a symmetry axis at X = 0, because the cylinder has a central hole and the axis is outside the modeled annular cross-section.

Model parameters:
- Material: linear elastic steel
  - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa
  - Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3
- Element type: PLANE183 with axisymmetric option enabled
- Mesh: global element size 5 mm

Boundary conditions and load:
- Inner cylindrical surface at X = 25 mm: apply an internal pressure of 10 MPa acting on the cylinder wall.
- Outer cylindrical surface at X = 50 mm: free surface.
- Axial faces:
  - At Y = 0 mm: constrain axial displacement UY = 0.
  - At Y = 10 mm: constrain axial displacement UY = 0.
- Do not constrain radial displacement UX on the inner or outer cylindrical surfaces.

Analysis type:
- Static structural analysis.

Save requirements:
- Use C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop as the ANSYS working directory.
- Save the database file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\apdl_cylinder.db
- Save the structural result file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\apdl_cylinder.rst
